page.layout: One printed page (left-hand page of the opening, number 186). Running head at top centre. Text in one column, with notes in the left margin beside the paragraphs. The narrow strip at the far right edge is the neighbouring page and is not transcribed. Catchwords at bottom right.

main_text.p: quorum antiquis rebus nihil omni-nò constat.
Insulae celebriores.Insulae Aiti, Cuba, Jamaica, Borriquen, celebriora regna habuerunt.
Insula Aiti V regna complecte-batur: sed pauca nobis de illorum rebus innotuêre, nisi ea, quae circa adventum Hispanorum in regiones eas acciderunt.
In Septentrione Imperium Mexicanum, ad Meridiem Cu-sconicum[?] omnium amplissima & cultissima fuerunt.Imperia amplissima.
r. Mexicanum, cujus notantur Origo &Mexicanorum origo deducitur à Navatlacis, qui fuerunt populus Americae Septentrionalis, supra reli-quorum barbariem excultus. Hi Na-

page.notes: The right edge shows the neighbouring page's text, which is not transcribed. "Cu-sconicum" is hard to read: the long s and tilde over the o are uncertain. The running head "Americanæ" ends in a letter that may be æ. The catchword "Hi Na-" is at the foot; "Hi" sits at the line end beside "excultus." and may be read as the catchword. The "r." in the Explic. line and in the left note is uncertain. The left margin note "r. Mexicanum, cujus notantur Origo &" is printed as shown.
